newsitem.title: USA: Congress delays final votes on budget, flood aid.
newsitem.headline: Congress delays final votes on budget, flood aid.

text.p: House Majority Leader Dick Armey announced Thursday Congress will not take final votes until June on either legislation to provide disaster relief to flooded states or on the balanced budget plan.

Armey, Republican of Texas, said difficulties between the House and Senate in resolving differences in the legislation prevented final action before Congress adjourned for a one-week recess. Congress is to return June 3.

"It is with deep regret and sense of apology that I inform members we are unable to do further work this evening on legislative business," Armey told the House after conferring with lawmakers who represent the flood-stricken states of the upper Midwest.
Several of the minority Democrats said they would object to vote for the adjournment resolution, a situation which could set off a political struggle on the House floor.

"We were unable to come to resolution of differences of the (flood relief) bill," House Appropriations Committee chairman Bob Livingston, Republican of Louisiana said. He noted they had met for several days on the $8.4 billion supplemental appropriations.

Livingston said he had been told by federal agencies there was enough money in the pipeline to respond to flood victims for the next several weeks. The bill provides $5.5 billion in disaster relief funds for 33 states, $1.9 billion to pay for U.S. military operations in Bosnia and the Gulf, and money for other projects.
